findings.section: Numbers that decide answers, A-list (also 1-fast.md Standard or FIFO queue table and its deciding question)
findings.quote: | [300 messages per second](...), [3,000 messages per second with batching](...) | Default FIFO queue throughput | More needs a standard queue |
findings.evidence: Facts sqs-fifo-ht-top-regions-70000-tps ('For high throughput mode ... US East (N. Virginia), US West (Oregon), and Europe (Ireland): Up to 70,000 transactions per second (TPS).') and sqs-change-fifo-high-throughput-quotas-raised-2022 (verified, in the canon). A FIFO queue in high throughput mode goes far beyond 3,000 messages per second, so 'More needs a standard queue' is false. On the exam it leads her to drop FIFO when a stem needs order and a high rate. The 1-fast table and its deciding question ('or is the highest throughput with idempotent consumers enough?') also present the default as the FIFO limit. Fix: 'More: high throughput mode for FIFO queues, or a standard queue when order does not matter', with the fact link, and add one line on high throughput mode to the FIFO subsection.
findings.resolution: fix-31: same fix as claims-02: A-list 'More: high throughput mode'; FIFO step 4 names high throughput mode with [70,000 transactions per second] in three Regions; 1-fast throughput cell and deciding question no longer present the default as the FIFO limit.

findings.quote: messaging-q011 verified pass 2 multi 3.2 fifo-group-id-per-customer; messaging-q021 verified pass 2 single 2.1 scheduler-vs-delay-queue; messaging-q006 verified edited-pass 2 single 2.1 eventbridge-rule-for-aws-service-events
findings.evidence: FREQUENCY.md row 12 (SQS): 'Buffering DB writes, Standard vs FIFO, visibility timeout, DLQ, long polling, retention period'; row 18: 'EventBridge rules and schedules'; comparison table: 'SQS Standard vs FIFO | Strict ordering and exactly-once processing → FIFO'. The 18 shipped questions have no FIFO ordering question, no schedule question and no question about an EventBridge rule for an AWS service event. Three verified questions that cover exactly these topics (q011, q021, q006) passed the blind panel but are not set to ready, while q005 (see exam-05) ships. Traps messaging-trap-fifo-global-order, messaging-trap-delay-queue-days and messaging-trap-build-own-change-detection therefore have no shipped question. Fix: set q011, q021 and q006 to ready (q set-status), and retire q005 if the count must stay at 18. With q011, the multi-response count is 3, inside the 2 to 3 range.
findings.resolution: fix-31: q011, q021 and q006 set to ready (all passed the panel); q005 retired (exam-05); to keep exactly 9 core and 9 extended, q003 (receive-does-not-delete, still taught by task t02) and q016 (sns-to-sqs-queue-policy, still taught by task t03) set back to verified as spares. q lint 31 --ship: ok, 18 ready, multi 3, twin pairs 3. No question was edited or reset.

findings.section: Shipped question set: long polling and Lambda with SQS
findings.quote: Consumers poll the queue and long polling waits for messages to arrive (3 min)
findings.evidence: FREQUENCY.md row 12 lists long polling, and row 6 (Lambda) lists 'SQS→Lambda'. No question of chapter 31 tests long polling ('reduce empty receives / cost' signal, fact sqs-faq-long-polling-fewer-empty-receives-lower-cost). The only Lambda event source mapping question (q014, partial batch response) was rejected, so trap messaging-trap-lambda-retries-failed-only and the six-times visibility rule (fact lambda-sqs-visibility-six-times-timeout) have no question. Write one replacement for each and send them to the blind panel.
findings.resolution: fix-31: not done in this stage. New questions need a writer and a full three-lens blind round (verify-questions), which the fix stage does not run; the shipped set already meets the deep counts. Long polling and the Lambda partial batch response stay taught in 2-deep (exam signal, exam trap, Stop and answer). Recommended for the next question round of chapter 31 (candidates: empty receives -> long polling; one failed message in a batch -> ReportBatchItemFailures).

findings.section: Signals and traps, row 'process in order; no duplicates'
findings.quote: | "process in order; no duplicates" | an SQS FIFO queue, one message group ID per entity | ... | order does not matter: a standard queue |
findings.evidence: The 'But not if' contradicts the stem phrase it guards ('process in order'), so it never fires. The guards that hold are in the chapter's own facts and questions: duplicates that come from outside the queue or after the window (fact sqs-fifo-deduplication-interval-5-minutes; Question 7 shows a FIFO queue fails there, so an idempotent consumer is needed), and order needed across several readers with replay (fact sqs-faq-kinesis-streams-realtime-and-replay → Kinesis Data Streams). Suggested guard: 'repeats arrive hours later, or several readers must replay: an idempotent consumer, or Kinesis Data Streams'.
findings.resolution: fix-31: 'But not if' is now 'repeats come hours later: an idempotent consumer' (the Kinesis part is left out to keep Signals and traps near its word cap; the SQS / MQ / Kinesis compare table covers replay).

findings.quote: Which AWS service provides this publish/subscribe model?
findings.evidence: The stem names the answer's own category ('publish/subscribe model'), and the key's explanation names that phrase as the deciding phrase. This trains keyword matching, not finding the constraint (READER.md: 'Train her to find the constraint in the stem'). The question asks for a service, but the options are designs. The Scheduler option is not plausible: nothing in the stem is about time. Real items describe the need ('each must receive every event') and do not name the pattern. Retire q005 in favour of q011, q021 or q006 (exam-02), or rewrite the last sentence to 'Which solution meets these requirements?' and replace the Scheduler distractor with an EventBridge Pipes or Kinesis option.
findings.resolution: fix-31: q005 retired (q set-status retired, reason recorded); a stem rewrite would change what the solvers see and need a new blind round, and the chapter has enough verified questions (exam-02).

findings.section: Signals and traps, row 'a message fails again and again; poison message'
findings.quote: | FIFO order must hold: it can [break the exact order of messages or operations](../facts/sqs.md#sqs-dlq-with-fifo-can-break-order) |
findings.evidence: Fact sqs-dlq-with-fifo-can-break-order is real ('Don't use a dead-letter queue with a FIFO queue if you don't want to break the exact order'). But the chapter also teaches that FIFO dead-letter queues are normal: fact sqs-dlq-type-must-match-source-queue-type, FAQ 5, a Stop and answer about orders.fifo, a Changed recently entry on FIFO dead-letter queue redrive, and Recap 2, which repeats the guard. An exam stem with a FIFO queue and poison messages expects a FIFO dead-letter queue. As the only guard, this row can make her reject the right answer. Narrow it: 'the stem says no message may ever leave its group's order (even a failed one)', or use a guard that decides more often: 'messages are processed twice because the job outlasts the visibility timeout: raise the timeout' (Question 6 and Question 8).
findings.resolution: fix-31: the row's 'But not if' is now 'the job outlasts the visibility timeout: raise the timeout', and Recap 2's answer matches ('Not if the job outlasts the visibility timeout: then raise the timeout.'). The FIFO order guard is gone from 1-fast.

findings.section: Signals and traps, row 'react to an AWS service event or a SaaS event'
findings.quote: | an **EventBridge rule** | ... | many phones or email addresses: SNS |
findings.evidence: If the stem says 'react to an AWS service event' and 'notify many phones or email addresses', the answer is both services: an EventBridge rule with an SNS topic as its target (fact eventbridge-faq-customers-use-sns-as-rule-target-to-filter-and-fan-out, and verified question q006: EC2 stop event → rule → email and Lambda). This guard says SNS instead of EventBridge, which is wrong for that stem. Write: 'the events come only from your own application and go to many phones: SNS alone (Question 15)'.
findings.resolution: fix-31: 'But not if' is now 'your own events go to thousands of phones: SNS'.

findings.section: Choose it or not, SQS SNS or EventBridge, Deciding question
findings.quote: **Deciding question:** Does one consumer pull at its own pace, must every subscriber get a copy now, or must a rule pick targets by content?
findings.evidence: SNS also picks receivers by content: fact sns-faq-message-filtering-subscribers-receive-subset, and since 2022 by the payload (fact sns-change-payload-based-filtering-2022). So 'by content' does not separate SNS from EventBridge. The chapter's own twin pair (Questions 11 and 15) shows what decides: where the events come from (AWS services or SaaS partners → EventBridge, facts eventbridge-default-bus-receives-aws-service-events and eventbridge-faq-eventbridge-only-service-integrating-directly-with-saas-partners) and how many endpoints (thousands of phones → SNS, fact sns-faq-sns-recommended-for-high-fan-out-thousands-or-millions). Rewrite: '... must every subscriber get a copy now, or do the events come from AWS services or SaaS partners?'
findings.resolution: fix-31: deciding question rewritten as suggested.

findings.section: SQS stores each message ... / Changed recently (1-fast.md)
findings.quote: > **The exam probably expects:** the old limit, with large payloads in Amazon S3. Prefer an option that is right under both values.
findings.evidence: The pattern that the Changed recently note says the exam expects is never taught. Fact sqs-extended-client-max-payload (and sns-extended-client-library-2gb) is in the canon. Older exam items ask what to do with messages larger than the queue limit: store the payload in Amazon S3 and send a reference, with the Extended Client Library. Add a 3-line Go deeper block or one A-list row in Numbers that decide answers, with these facts.
findings.resolution: fix-31: B-list row added: '[2 GB](sqs-extended-client-max-payload) | Payload in Amazon S3 with the Extended Client Library'. A B-list row, not an A-list row: the A-list is at its 8-row maximum, and an A-list fact would need a number card (C204).

findings.section: Failed deliveries are retried and then dropped unless a dead-letter queue catches them, step 1
findings.quote: To SQS and Lambda, SNS tries [100,015 times](...); to email and text message (SMS), it makes [50 attempts](...).
findings.evidence: Facts sns-retry-aws-managed-total-attempts ('Total attempts: 100,015 times, over 23 days') and sns-retry-customer-managed-total-attempts ('50 attempts, over 6 hours'). Exam stems give an outage time ('down for several hours', 'for a day'), so the time window decides, not the attempt count, and the text drops it. The most examined case, an HTTP/S subscription, is missing from the subsection, although Check 3 and Questions 4, 9 and 14 depend on it (fact sns-retry-http-total-retry-time-max, 3,600 seconds). Add the two time windows and an HTTP/S line.
findings.resolution: fix-31: step 1 now 'To SQS and Lambda, SNS retries [over 23 days]; to email and text message (SMS), [over 6 hours]; to HTTP/S, at most [3,600 seconds].' (attempt counts dropped to stay within the 4,500-word file limit).

findings.section: Questions 6 and 8 (messaging-q002 and its twin messaging-q009)
findings.evidence: SPEC.json questions.twin_min_questions_between = 3. Only Question 7 is between the twins, and both have the same four options in the same order, so she answers Question 8 from memory of Question 6 and not from the deciding phrase. Move q009 at least three questions later (q001/q007 and q013/q018 already meet the rule).
findings.resolution: fix-31: the q002 item was moved to the front of data/31-messaging/questions.json (item bytes unchanged, no verification touched). Printed order after sync: q002 is Question 3 and q009 Question 8 (4 between); q001/q007 have 3 between; q013/q018 have 4.

findings.quote: All events come from the company's own order application. Every event must also reach the mobile phones of thousands of field agents by SMS within seconds.
findings.evidence: The twin_rules in SPEC.json say the twin line quotes 'the changed phrase'. This pair changes three things: the event sources, an added SMS requirement, and the removed sentence 'Each service selects events by fields inside the event detail'. The reader cannot tell which change flips the key. Without the SMS sentence, both EventBridge and SNS fit q018, so the SMS sentence decides, and the source change only removes the SaaS signal. Keep q013's sentences and change one phrase only. For example, replace the sources sentence with 'All events come from the company's own order application, and every event must also reach thousands of field agents by SMS'.
findings.resolution: fix-31: not changed. A stem edit of a verified question resets its verification (TOOLS-rules R5) and would need a new blind round; both questions passed the panel unanimously and the key of each is unambiguous. The q013 twin line quotes the changed sentences in full. The strict-twin check (Q114 strict form) is 'review until implemented' (R11). Recommended for a later question round.

findings.section: A filter policy decides which messages reach each subscription
findings.quote: | Filter on attributes | [Attribute-based message filtering is free](../facts/sns.md#sns-pricing-attribute-filtering-free) |
findings.evidence: Fact sns-change-payload-based-filtering-2022 ('Payload-based filtering lets you filter messages based on the message payload ... November 22, 2022'; the scope defaults to MessageAttributes). The section presents attribute filtering only. Older questions may assume that SNS filters only on message attributes, which is the condition for a 'Changed recently' note under RULINGS hard rule 7. Add one line: a filter policy can match message attributes (the default scope) or the message body.
findings.resolution: fix-31: filter step 2 adds 'It reads the attributes by default ([MessageAttributes](sns-change-payload-based-filtering-2022)), or the message body.'; fan-out step 3 names attributes or body (claims-08). No Changed recently entry: the 1-fast section is at its 120-word cap.

findings.quote: Keep the standard queue and fix the partner system alone, because a standard queue delivers each message exactly once and in order.
findings.evidence: Both options give a false reason inside the option text ('... because an SNS topic sends every message to every subscription' in Question 16), so a reader who knows the basic fact removes them at once and the item gives no practice in judgment. Real exam distractors are workable designs that fail the qualifier. Make each a plausible design with no reason clause, for example 'Keep the standard queue and add a uniqueness check to the partner system'.
findings.resolution: fix-31: not changed. Rewriting an option of a verified question changes what the blind solvers saw and resets verification (R5); the key of both questions stays right and both passed the panel. Recorded for the next question round.

findings.section: Numbers that decide answers, A-list row 14 days
findings.quote: | [14 days](../facts/sqs.md#sqs-message-retention-range) | Longest retention period | A longer outage needs Amazon S3 |
findings.evidence: 'A longer outage needs Amazon S3' is not a pattern any question in the chapter teaches; Question 12's twin uses 'copy the failed messages to Amazon S3' for keeping messages longer than 14 days. Write it as the exam frames it: 'Keeping messages longer than 14 days: copy them to Amazon S3.'
findings.resolution: fix-31: the row's decider is now 'Longer: copy to Amazon S3'.
